subject: GrovePay renewal + expansion: pricing harmonization and commit uplift
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@grovepay.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + expansion ask (usage spike next quarter)

Marcus —

Thanks for all your support this year. We’ve been reviewing usage forecasts at GrovePay and we expect a material uplift starting next quarter as we roll out a new fraud-detection flow. Before we lock into the renewal, procurement asked us to confirm whether we can get a 12-month price hold and a short-term expansion path (roughly 2x committed capacity for the first 3 months, then step down).

Key asks: 
- 12-month price hold on existing committed unit price (or an agreed rollback trigger)
- One-time expansion uplift (2x) for Q4 with credits applied to the renewal
- Clarity on overage handling and temporary burst pools

I attached a usage extract for the last three months. Can Redwood outline options so we can present to finance and procurement next week?

Appreciate an estimate asap — we have an internal steering meeting on Mon.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Engineering, GrovePay

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + expansion ask (usage spike next quarter)

Sanjay —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the usage extract. We’ve reviewed the file and see the projected uplift you mentioned. I’ll loop in Laura (your AE) and Soojin (SE) to put together a few concrete options:

1) Short-term expansion credit + phased commit uplift (recommended)
2) Larger annual commit with deeper discount + price hold clause
3) Pay-as-you-go burst with capped overage rate for first 90 days

Can you confirm the approximate peak tokens/day and whether the 2x is expected to be sustained for the full month or just spikes? That will help us size the burst pool and credit schedule.

We’ll aim to send a proposal by Monday EOD so you have something for finance/procurement.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: GrovePay renewal negotiation — proposal framing (notes)

Team — quick internal thread to align before we send the proposal to GrovePay. Below is my read and suggested structure. Keep replies short (we’ll synthesize into the doc).

Context: GrovePay expects a ~2x token/throughput spike for Q4 tied to a product launch. Procurement wants stable pricing for 12 months; they’re open to a commit uplift if offsets are provided.

Proposed structure (tiered, conservative above-market credits to protect margins):
- Option A (Preferred): 12-month renewal, +30% base commit (phased: 15% at M1, additional 15% at M4) + 3-month expansion credit that covers the incremental usage above their baseline up to 2x. 8% discount on committed tier for the term; price hold for 6 months (then review).
- Option B: 12-month renewal, +60% upfront commit, 12% discount, no separate expansion credit but lower overage rate cap for first 90 days.
- Option C: 6-month interim contract (price hold), then renegotiate — used if procurement demands shorter legal window.

Operational asks for SE: Soojin — can you confirm implications for KV cache residency and estimated GPU-hours per 1M tokens at their current model? Also list assumptions on burst latency SLA.
Finance ops: Ben — want to confirm discount floor we can give (target gross margin >= 55% post-credit).

Next steps: draft MAProposal_v3 with numbers and fallback language (rollback trigger for price hold if usage drops >40% vs forecast). Attach draft and iterate.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@grovepay.com>, Melanie Chu <melanie@grovepay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: GrovePay renewal + Q4 expansion (proposal attached)

Sanjay / Melanie —

Appreciate the context and the usage extract. Please find attached our proposal (GrovePay_MAProposal_v3.pdf) with three options summarized below. I’ll follow up with Laura to schedule a 30-minute walk-through this week.

Summary (high-level):
- Preferred option (A): 12-month renewal; phased commit uplift (15% immediate, +15% at month 4); 3-month expansion credit that reimburses incremental usage above baseline up to 2x. 8% standard discount on the committed tiers. Temporary price hold: 6 months firm, then reassess vs actuals. Rollback trigger: if usage is >40% below forecast for two consecutive months we will re-open pricing discussions (limited to a price adjustment not to exceed 6%).
- Option B: 12-month renewal with larger upfront commit (+60%) and 12% discount. No separate expansion credit; instead a capped overage at a reduced rate for the first 90 days.
- Option C: 6-month bridge renewal with strict price hold then re-evaluation.

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling Redwood’s short-term burst pool rather than immediate permanent commit to avoid long-term exposure.
- We can provide initial burst capacity at 2x for up to 90 days via credits; credits can be drawn against renewal invoice.

Attachments: GrovePay_MAProposal_v3.pdf (detailed pricing, legal fallback language), usage_report_q2_2026.csv (your file).

Related links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/GP-2026-RNW-045 ; Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GrovePayProposal

If this looks directionally correct, let’s get a short call on Wed to review the numbers and finalize the version for procurement.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192
attachment: GrovePay_MAProposal_v3.pdf
From: Melanie Chu <melanie@grovepay.com>

Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: GrovePay renewal + Q4 expansion (proposal attached)

Marcus —

Thanks for the detailed options and for getting that over quickly. Option A aligns best with what Finance wants — the phased commit + expansion credit is sensible. A few follow-ups from procurement before we lock: 

1) Can you add explicit contract language for the rollback trigger (exact clause wording + process for dispute resolution)? Procurement wants a 30-day notice window before any price adjustment.
2) We need a PO-friendly invoice cadence (Net 30) and a statement that credits applied to the renewal can be itemized on the invoice.
3) Will Redwood accept our standard security addendum (we’ll route that via DocuSign once legal edits are done)?

CCing procurement to keep them in the loop. If you can incorporate those points and resend the doc, we can move to signature quickly. Also confirm the one-time onboarding credit that offsets initial integration costs (you mentioned a small credit — need $10k line item).

Melanie Chu
Procurement Lead, GrovePay
procurement@grovepay.com
